description: What the service would do with a job or a set, running nothing: the method and why, the memory, the estimated time and energy (each with its basis: this service's own timings and readings where it has them, otherwise the planner's nominal rate, and no energy figure without readings), the bounds that apply, where you stand against your limits, and whether the service would take it now, or the refusal it would give, with its code. Takes what run_quantum_circuit or run_quantum_set takes. It counts as one submission.

amplitudes.description: Basis states to give amplitudes of: one character per qubit, qubit n-1 first, e.g. "0011".

compile.description: Compile the program first (as compile_qasm does) and run the compiled circuit: with basis clifford_t it runs bit-exact, and the result's `compiled` states its distance from the program.

basis.description: clifford_t (default): every rotation off the multiples of π/4 written as a Clifford+T word within its share of epsilon; standard: nothing approximated.

dd.description: Dynamical decoupling in each window where a qubit idles long enough, checked to change nothing without noise.

epsilon.description: The most the output may differ from the program in the operator norm, up to a global phase, shared by its rotations (default 1e-6).

level.description: 0: lower and approximate; 1 (default): also checked rewrites and phase folding; 2: also one- and two-qubit resynthesis.

twirl.description: Twirl each two-qubit Clifford gate with Paulis from a seeded stream: true, or {"seed": N}. One seed is one instance, checked to be the same circuit.

fabric.description: Where the statevector method's state runs: auto (the default: on a member only where the committed measurements show it faster than the host's CPU for the job's size and fusion, otherwise the CPU), cpu, accelerator (any certified accelerator member), a member's id or key, or a list of members, a power of two of them, the state split by its top qubits into one partition on each; a pauli job's sum of terms runs on the member accelerator or its id or key names. Every member placed is certified bit-exact against the CPU, so the answers are the CPU's; the result's `fabric` names where the state ran, sealed by the receipt. A placement the service cannot honour is refused (J013): it places only on its CPU.

anyOf.description: One of distribution, equivalent, prepares or sampled; with note, name, and "require": "proof" (evidence then counts as unchecked).

alpha.description: For a sampled intent: the significance level, as 0.01.

distribution.description: The exact distribution of the measured bits, keyed by the classical bits with the highest bit first, as {"00": 0.5, "11": 0.5}.

equivalent.description: A reference program's text: the same circuit up to a global phase, by the equivalence ladder.

prepares.description: A reference program's text: the same state from |0…0⟩, the same qubits measured into the same bits.

sampled.description: A distribution the program's samples are held to: the program run as the job runs it for `shots` at `seed`, and the counts tested by `test` at the significance level `alpha` (all three required). Evidence, never proof.

seed.description: For a sampled intent: the sampling seed (default: the job's).

shots.description: For a sampled intent: the samples the test takes.

test.description: For a sampled intent: Pearson's chi-squared test, or the G-test (the likelihood ratio).

tolerance.description: For a distribution: the total variation distance it is held within (default 1e-9).

items.description: One of distribution, equivalent, prepares or sampled; with note, name, and "require": "proof" (evidence then counts as unchecked).

alpha.description: For a sampled intent: the significance level, as 0.01.

distribution.description: The exact distribution of the measured bits, keyed by the classical bits with the highest bit first, as {"00": 0.5, "11": 0.5}.

equivalent.description: A reference program's text: the same circuit up to a global phase, by the equivalence ladder.

prepares.description: A reference program's text: the same state from |0…0⟩, the same qubits measured into the same bits.

sampled.description: A distribution the program's samples are held to: the program run as the job runs it for `shots` at `seed`, and the counts tested by `test` at the significance level `alpha` (all three required). Evidence, never proof.

seed.description: For a sampled intent: the sampling seed (default: the job's).

shots.description: For a sampled intent: the samples the test takes.

test.description: For a sampled intent: Pearson's chi-squared test, or the G-test (the likelihood ratio).

tolerance.description: For a distribution: the total variation distance it is held within (default 1e-9).

intent.description: What the program must do, checked by the engine with the run: the result's `verdict` states how far it checked (proof, evidence, executed, parsed, refused) and whether the intent holds, sealed by the receipt.

method.description: Leave as auto unless you need a particular method; pulse runs a pulse program (OpenPulse calibrations on physical qubits, see pulse_schedule) under the pulse options, its error bounded.

factors.description: zne: odd whole numbers (default 1, 3, 5); pea: factors from 1 to 10 (default 1, 1.5, 2).

keep.description: cdr: non-Clifford gates each training circuit keeps (default 2, and always one fewer than the program has).

learn_shots.description: pea, pec: shots per depth of the cycle benchmarking that learns the noise (default 60000).

shots.description: Shots per circuit (default 10000; 2000 per sampled circuit for pec).

mitigate.description: Mitigate the job's expectation values (or, for readout, its counts) under its own noise: zne (the whole program folded U(U†U)^k and extrapolated), pea (the noise learned as a sparse Pauli–Lindblad model and amplified), pec (the learned channels inverted and sampled), cdr (a line fitted over near-Clifford training circuits), vd (two copies), readout (the counts' flips inverted). Needs noise and observables (shots for readout), at most 8 qubits. The result's `mitigation` gives raw and mitigated values with standard errors, the ideal value (known because this is a simulation), the method's bias and variance assumptions and its cost. A method's name, or an object.

noise.description: Optional noise, each a probability: depolarizing_1q, depolarizing_2q, amplitude_damping, dephasing (after each gate on its qubits), readout (each measured bit).

observables.description: Pauli strings to take expectation values of, e.g. ["Z0", "Z0 Z1", "X2 Y3"]. Qubits count from 0.

options.description: Advanced, per method: max_bond (mps), threshold and max_terms (pauli), fusion (statevector), trajectories.

params.description: A value for each of the program's parameters (input float theta;, input angle phi;), as {"theta": 0.3}: bound exactly before the program is read; a parameter left without one is refused (J050). In a sweep, the parameters it fixes.

programs.description: The set's programs: each a program's text, or a job ({"qasm", …}) whose own fields win over the set's.

pulse.description: A pulse run's options (method "pulse"): the sample period, the levels kept, the tolerance on the stated error, the steps a sample is divided into, each qubit's parameters, static couplings, and ports beyond the names d0, m0, a0.

levels.description: Levels kept per qubit (default 2; 3 shows leakage).

ports.description: Ports by name: what each is for and the qubit it reaches.

rabi_mhz.description: Its Rabi frequency at full amplitude, MHz.

qubits.description: Each qubit's parameters by its index, over the target's and the defaults.

substeps.description: Steps per sample (default: chosen so each step times the generator's norm is at most 0.5).

tolerance.description: The most the stated error may be (default 1e-6): a run whose bound and rounding estimate pass it is refused, naming the steps that would meet it.

qasm.description: The program, OpenQASM 3 (or 2), read as the whole language: registers, aliases and slices; the standard gates, `U` and `gphase`; user `gate` definitions and `def` subroutines, inlined; every modifier (`ctrl @`, `negctrl @`, `inv @`, `pow(k) @`) on any gate, lowered exactly; classical types (int, uint, float, angle, complex, bool, bit, arrays), their arithmetic and built-in functions, computed on reading; `for`, `while`, `switch`, `break`, `continue`; measurement and `reset` anywhere; classical control on measured bits (`if (c[0]) x q[1];`, `if (c >= 2) { … } else { … }`, `&&`, `||`); a `while` on measured bits takes `@wai.max_iterations N` before it. `output` declarations come back in the result; `delay`, `box` and `stretch` are carried and labelled as not applied; `defcal` and `cal` are kept, not run. A program that measures in the middle or acts on what it measured runs on statevector or stabilizer: counts split their shots at each measurement; expectation values are exact, of the state before the final measurements. What the reader refuses comes back with a code, as `[Q103]`; qasm_diagnostics says what each code means.

repair.description: Repair the program first, on the lines its diagnostics flag alone (as repair_qasm does): true, or the choices {"max_iterations": N, "dyadic_bits": K, "sizes": {"q": 3}}. The result's `repaired` holds the program that ran and each repair.

seed.description: Sampling seed (default 1); the same job and seed give the same counts.

shots.description: Measurement shots. Default 1024 when no observables or amplitudes are asked for.

source.description: The program in another format, in place of qasm: read to the job's qasm before the job is read (a module that does not read is refused with the reader's code, Q700 to Q721), the request keeping its source.

program.description: The program's text: QIR (LLVM text) or OpenQASM.

program_base64.description: The program's bytes as base64: jeff.

sweep.description: Each input of qasm and its values: every combination runs, the names in sorted order, the first varying slowest; an integer input's values are whole numbers.

target.description: A device target: a built-in target's name (list_targets) or a target document (wai.quantum.target/1). The program is then compiled to its gates, placed where it is most likely to succeed and simulated under its noise, its hash in the receipt; not with noise or amplitudes. The service reads the document given and fetches nothing.

anyOf.description: What the service would do with a job or a set, running nothing: the plan's method and why, its qubits, memory and work, the estimated time and energy (each with its basis, or why there is none), the bounds that apply, where the client stands against its limits, each item of a set, and whether the service would take it now, or the refusal it would give.

accepted.description: Whether the service would take it now, by every limit.

bounds.description: The bounds that apply here: memory, time, queue and items of a set.

client.description: Where the client stands: its active jobs, the memory they hold, the submissions left in its window and when the window resets.

energy.description: The estimated energy, never a reading of this job: microjoules, its provenance and basis, or why there is none.

items.description: A set: each item's plan and estimates.

refusal.description: For a refused job: its message and its codes.

status.description: The HTTP status a refusal would carry.

target.description: A job on a device target: the target the plan placed it on.

time.description: The estimated time: seconds and its basis, or null and why, with the most the job may take.

verdict.description: How far the engine checked an answer about a program, as one level of an ordered ladder (wai-quantum://docs/verdicts): refused, parsed, executed, evidence, proof. A level says how far the engine checked, not that the answer is good: holds says whether the intents held (true, false, or null when none was decided). A job's result carries one under verdict when the job gives an intent or asks for one, and the receipt seals it; both MCP servers state one beside every answer about a program.

critique.description: The program's smells, each with its lines.

executed.description: The method that ran and its accuracy class, and the distance a compile put between the program and what ran.

items.description: One intent's check: what it asked, whether it held, how strong the check was and how it was made.

distribution.description: The program's distribution, when its outcomes are few enough to list.

fit.description: A sampled intent: the test, its statistic, degrees of freedom and p-value, the level, and whether it rejected.

method.description: A sampled intent: the method the samples were run by.

outcomes.description: The outcomes the distribution holds, or the samples' distinct outcomes.

parsed.description: Whether the reader took the program, and its warnings and notes with their codes, or its refusal.

items.description: One of the reader's diagnostics: its code, what happens to the construct it is about, its message (without the line or the code), and where it stands.

text.description: The refusal as the reader wrote it, with its line and code.

rank.description: The level's place on the ladder, from 0 (refused) to 4 (proof).

refusal.description: For a refused job: its message and its codes.

repairs.description: Each edit a repair made, with the code it answered and the lines it changed.

statement.description: The level in one plain line.
